title: Privacy policy
text:
1. Purpose of this privacy policy
The Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML) Working Group at the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) is committed to protecting your personal data. This privacy policy explains what personal data may be processed when you visit this website, how it is used, and what rights you have.

title: Privacy policy
text:
2. Collection of data
Since this website is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages, we do not actively collect personal data. However, the following data may be processed by our hosting provider as part of standard operation:

Log data: Information such as IP address, browser type, operating system, referring URL, pages visited, and timestamps may be logged by GitHub Pages.
Cookies: This site does not set its own tracking cookies. GitHub may use cookies as part of providing and securing their services.

Please refer to the GitHub Privacy Statement for details on their handling of log data and cookies.

title: Privacy policy
text:
3. Use of data
We do not use personal data for analytics, marketing, or profiling. Any data processed by GitHub (e.g., server logs) is used to operate and secure the hosting platform.

title: Privacy policy
text:
4. Sharing your data
We do not sell, lease, or share personal data. GitHub, as the hosting provider, may process data according to their privacy policy.

title: Privacy policy
text:
5. Data subject rights (GDPR)
Under the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:

Right to access (Art. 15)
Right to rectification (Art. 16)
Right to erasure (Art. 17)
Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18)
Right to object (Art. 21)
Right to data portability (Art. 20)

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77).

title: Privacy policy
text:
6. Data retention
We do not retain personal data through this website. Any log data processed by GitHub is retained according to GitHub’s policies.

title: Privacy policy
text:
7. Third-party services and links
This site may link to third-party websites. We are not responsible for their privacy practices. Please review the privacy policies of those websites.

title: Privacy policy
text:
8. Security measures
This static website does not operate its own user database. GitHub Pages provides operational and platform security. See GitHub’s Security overview for more details.

title: Privacy policy
text:
9. Updates to this policy
We may update this privacy policy to reflect changes in legal requirements or website functionality. Updates will be published on this page.

title: Privacy policy
text:
10. Contact
If you have questions about this privacy policy, please contact:

Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) e.V.
Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML) Working Group

title: Upcoming Quarto Workshop at iEMSs 2026
text:
We are excited to announce that the DML group will host a workshop at the International Environmental Modelling and Software Society (iEMSs) 2026 conference in Dublin over the 12-16th July.
The workshop “One Publishing Tool to Rule Them All: Quarto for Documentation, Presentations, Manuscripts and Outreach”, which is being prepared in collaboration with researchers from ETH Zurich will explore Quarto as a unified solution for academic communication. Quarto can generate multiple output formats — PDF, HTML, LaTeX, and DOCX — from a single source document while supporting executable code in Python, R, Julia, and Observable. Through short presentations and guided exercises, participants will learn to produce documentation, reproducible journal articles, presentations, outreach websites, and interactive dashboards — all from one tool.
We will make the content from both the workshop available online prior to the conference, so stay tuned for more updates!

text: We recognise that we cannot be experts in every topic and it is OK to inform service users of this. Reproducibility for Everyone (R4Everyone) - A community-driven initiative to promote reproducibility in scientific research through training, resources, and advocacy.

title: DML Presents at IAT Kickoff Meeting
text: In March 2026 the Innovation Center for Agricultural System Transformation (IAT) was officially launched, with two days of events at the Futurium in Berlin as well as the ZALF campus in Müncheberg. The focus of the 2nd day was on connecting researchers working on similar topics within the IAT from both ZALF and the partner institutions. We were fortunate to have an opportunity to present our concept for how the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs group (DML) will provide a three pillar approach of services to support IAT researchers and living labs in their data and modelling needs. The slides we presented are available below, and we are looking forward to engaging with the IAT and broader ZALF community in the coming months to produce some real outputs from collaborations to serve as a showcase for the services we can provide.

title: DML at the FAIRagro Community Summit
text:
In March, DML working group members travelled to Frankfurt to attend the FAIRagro Community Summit. The event brought together the FAIRagro community to showcase the services and tools the consortium has been developing to advance Open and FAIR data practices in agricultural research.
FAIRagro is an NFDI consortium that has represented the agrosystems research community in Germany since 2023. With more than 30 partners, it is building a FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) research data management infrastructure — developing the tools and workflows needed to support Open Science and sustainable crop production.
The summit was a great opportunity to exchange ideas, hear about ongoing developments, and connect with others working on research data challenges in agriculture. We look forward to future collaboration with the FAIRagro consortium!

title: IAT ZALF Templates
text: This project delivered a collection of reusable document and presentation templates for the IAT working groups, covering both technical publishing pipelines (Quarto extensions) and traditional office formats (PowerPoint). All templates are available in a public GitHub repository at https://github.com/iat-dml/templates.

title: IAT ZALF Templates
text:
Quarto Extensions
The core deliverables are four Quarto extensions that can be installed directly from the repository and used in any Quarto project. They are self-contained — logos, colour palettes, and fonts are all bundled inside the _extensions/ folder, so documents render consistently regardless of the local environment.

ZALF Internal Documents
A Quarto Typst extension that renders .qmd files as branded ZALF PDF documents. The cover page places the ZALF and Leibniz Association logos at the top and bottom respectively, with a grey band across the middle carrying the document title, date, and an optional cover image. Subsequent pages use running headers, styled H1–H4 headings, coloured bullet lists, and striped tables — all drawn from the official ZALF green palette (#46A84F).



Cover page of the ZALF internal document template


quarto use template iat-dml/templates/zalf-internal-typst


IAT Internal Documents
A companion Typst extension for IAT internal PDF documents. It follows the same cover-page and body layout as the ZALF template but swaps in the IAT brand palette, the combined ZALF/IAT logo, and a branded footer banner with partner and funder logos.



Cover page of the IAT internal document template


quarto use template iat-dml/templates/iat-internal-typst


IAT Presentations
A Quarto Revealjs extension for branded IAT HTML slide decks. The title slide uses a deep forest-green hero panel with white headings and the ZALF/IAT logo in the top-right corner. A full-width footer bar carries partner university logos and funder marks, ensuring compliance with grant acknowledgement requirements out of the box.



Title slide of the IAT Revealjs presentation template


quarto use template iat-dml/templates/iat-revealjs


DML Presentations
A Revealjs extension styled for the Data and Modelling Infrastructure (DML) working group. The theme reflects the DML visual identity: DM Serif Display for large headings, DM Sans for body text, a warm off-white paper background, and a teal-dark primary colour with green and olive accents. A persistent DML circular mark appears in the lower-right corner of every content slide and hides automatically in PDF exports.



Title slide of the DML Revealjs presentation template


quarto use template iat-dml/templates/dml-revealjs

title: MonksHillLabs Initiative
text:
MonksHillLabs is a collaborative research platform that provides shared computational infrastructure, data repositories, and development environments for landscape and land use modelling projects.
The initiative brings together researchers, data scientists, and software developers to co-create tools, standards, and workflows that advance data interoperability and reproducible research in landscape science.
Current activities include developing standardized data formats, building modular modelling components, and hosting hackathons and training workshops.
